nodes.label: Upstream Fork-Scope Policy
nodes.rationale: This is a template, not a collaborative product; upstream scope is intentionally narrow, so most feature requests end up as 'build this in your fork' rather than landing here.

nodes.label: Pinned Next/React/Tailwind
nodes.rationale: Next, React, and Tailwind are pinned exactly on purpose; let them flow through manual major bumps when we're ready.

nodes.label: Account-Scoped Tenancy
nodes.rationale: Every install is multi-tenant on the database side; every row is scoped to the account rather than the user, and WhatsApp config is one-per-account.

nodes.label: Upstream PR Policy
nodes.rationale: Template scope is intentionally narrow; security fixes and bug fixes land quickly, while new features, stack changes, and opinionated refactors belong in forks.

nodes.label: Why Fork (Template Philosophy)
nodes.rationale: Forking gives full ownership, full customisation, zero ops to start, and real security primitives; the stack is boring on purpose so the learning curve is short.

nodes.label: Read-Only by Default Safety Model
nodes.rationale: The server is read-only until you opt in, layered on top of the API key's own scopes; a read-only key plus read-only config means it physically cannot send anything.

nodes.label: Per-Key Rate Limits
nodes.rationale: Limiter is in-memory and per process; fine for a single-instance self-hosted deploy, but multi-instance scaling requires a shared store (Redis/Upstash).

nodes.label: Three-Layer Safety Model
nodes.rationale: Sending WhatsApp messages through an LLM is a real-world side effect, so the server layers three guards: read-only by default, API-key scopes, and explicit broadcast confirmation.
